Title and Summary

Lead Technology Risk Analyst

Overview

The Lead Technology Risk Analyst within the Program Controls, Operations & Modernization (ProCOM) Office is responsible for leading the implementation and execution of technology risk management, governance, controls, and operational resilience programs across Mastercard's technology organization. This role partners closely with technology, product, engineering, security, and business teams to identify, assess, monitor, and mitigate technology risks while strengthening control effectiveness and operational maturity.

The position serves as a key leader in advancing ProCOM's mission to deliver scalable governance, risk management, production readiness, and operational excellence capabilities. Through risk assessments, governance oversight, control monitoring, operational intelligence, and continuous improvement initiatives, this role helps ensure technology products and platforms are delivered with resiliency, reliability, and compliance while enabling informed risk-based decision making. The Lead, Technology Risk Manager plays a critical role in translating strategic risk objectives into actionable programs, measurable outcomes, and sustainable operational practices.

Role
- Lead the execution of technology risk management programs and initiatives across products, platforms, services, and technology domains.
- Facilitate technology risk identification, assessment, treatment, monitoring, and escalation processes to ensure risks are proactively managed and appropriately governed.
- Drive adoption of technology risk frameworks, policies, standards, and procedures across engineering and technology teams.
- Partner with product, engineering, operations, security, and risk stakeholders to evaluate control effectiveness and identify opportunities to strengthen operational resilience.
- Lead risk assessments, control reviews, operational readiness evaluations, and governance activities supporting strategic initiatives and technology changes.
- Monitor technology risk indicators, control metrics, issue remediation activities, and operational performance trends to identify emerging risks and systemic concerns.
- Develop executive-ready reporting, risk summaries, governance materials, and operational insights that support leadership decision-making.
- Coordinate technology risk governance forums and ensure action items, decisions, and risk mitigation activities are appropriately tracked and executed.
- Support audit, regulatory, compliance, and assurance activities by coordinating evidence collection, remediation planning, and stakeholder engagement.
- Identify recurring operational issues, control gaps, and process weaknesses and lead initiatives to improve risk management effectiveness.
- Drive automation and process improvements that reduce manual effort, enhance governance capabilities, and improve data quality and reporting accuracy.
- Leverage operational and risk data to develop meaningful insights, trends, and recommendations that support proactive risk management.
- Provide guidance and subject matter expertise to stakeholders on technology risk, governance, resilience, and control practices.
- Mentor and support team members while fostering a culture of accountability, collaboration, continuous improvement, and operational excellence.

All About You
- Experience in technology risk management, operational risk, governance, controls, cybersecurity, audit, compliance, technology operations, or related disciplines.
- Strong understanding of technology risk frameworks, risk assessment methodologies, control environments, and operational resilience principles.
- Demonstrated ability to identify, assess, and communicate technology and operational risks in a clear and business-focused manner.
- Experience leading risk assessments, control reviews, issue management activities, governance processes, and remediation efforts.
- Strong analytical and problem-solving skills with the ability to evaluate complex operational and technical situations and recommend practical solutions.
- Experience developing executive-level reporting, governance materials, dashboards, and risk intelligence presentations.
- Ability to analyze operational, risk, and performance data to identify trends, emerging risks, and opportunities for improvement.
- Strong stakeholder management skills with the ability to influence and collaborate effectively across business, technology, product, and control functions.

Corporate Security Responsibility

All activities involving access to Mastercard assets, information, and networks comes with an inherent risk to the organization and, therefore, it is expected that every person working for, or on behalf of, Mastercard is responsible for information security and must:

Abide by Mastercard’s security policies and practices;

Ensure the confidentiality and integrity of the information being accessed;

Complete all periodic mandatory security trainings in accordance with Mastercard’s guidelines.

ABOUT MISTRAL

Mistral provides full-stack AI solutions: from frontier models to developer tools, applications, and compute. Our teams are distributed between Europe, North America, Asia and the Middle East. We are creative, low-ego and team-spirited.

ABOUT THE JOB

Mistral is hiring a Head of FDE Learning Programs to build the learning system for one of the company’s fastest-growing organizations. Mistral is scaling its FDE organization from its first hire to several hundred Deployment Strategists and Applied AI Engineers within two years. Your mandate is to make capability grow as fast as headcount without lowering the bar for customer work.

You will own:

- Learning content: Build practical learning across three areas: technical skills, strategic and business capabilities, and product enablement.

- Onboarding: Build a clear path from a new hire’s first week to independent customer work.

- Technical bootcamps: Turn new products, research, and field methods into practical training for customer work.

- Strategic bootcamps: Empower client-facing teams of FDEs to drive business and strategic discussions and to set up for success large partnership programs with customers

- Program ownership: Own the roadmap, curriculum, contributor model, regional delivery, tools, measurement, and central team.

- Scaling: Launch useful programs now, then adapt them for larger cohorts without making the content generic or relying on a small group of experts.

- Team building: Launch the first programs, build a network of instructors, and hire the team needed to support several hundred FDEs.

- Cross-functional work: Work with functional managers, Product, Engineering, Science, People, GTM Enablement, DevRel, and regional leaders.

- Readiness standards: Ensure FDEs in every region meet the same standard, can find current material, learn from recent customer work, and understand expectations at the next career level.

- Knowledge structuration: Ensure internal resources are up to date and pushed to the right stakeholders with a knowledge management approach.

HOW WE WORK IN SOLUTIONS

- We care about people and outputs.

- What matters is what you ship, not the time you spend on it

- Bureaucracy is where urgency goes to vanish. You talk to whoever you need to talk to. The best idea wins, whether it comes from a principal engineer or someone in their first week.

- Always ask why. The best solutions come from deep understanding, not from copying what worked before

- We say what we mean. Feedback is direct, timely, and given because we care.

- No politics. Low ego, high standards.

- We embrace an unstructured environment and find joy in it.

You have helped build a learning, enablement, or capability function for a technical organization during rapid growth. You can start as the first dedicated owner, deliver useful programs immediately, and build the team and operating model needed to serve several hundred people.

-

- You are technically fluent enough to work credibly with AI engineers, Product, and Science, inspect the substance of a program, and challenge material that is unclear or outdated.

- You have designed programs that work across cohorts, regions, and experience levels without reducing the content to generic training.

-

- You can lead work across senior stakeholders, subject-matter experts, managers, and operational partners without relying on reporting lines.

- You can make firm trade-offs when hiring demand, expert capacity, and program quality compete for attention.

- You pay attention to the full learner experience, including communications, scheduling, practice, feedback, and manager follow-through.

- You use evidence to decide which programs to expand, revise, or stop.

- You communicate clearly with executives, managers, technical experts, and learners.

- You are fluent in English and can work with teams across regions and time zones.

IDEALLY, YOU HAVE

- Scaled a one-person or small learning function into a team and program that served hundreds of technical employees.

- Built onboarding that kept pace with rapid hiring in an engineering, FDE, solutions, consulting, or professional-services organization.

- Designed and operated technical bootcamps or other cohort-based learning programs.

- Worked in technical DevRel, developer education, or a related role built around demos, code examples, workshops, and practitioner communities.

- Used learning platforms, knowledge systems, AI coaches, or program-operations tooling.

Mistral is compressing years of organization growth into two. An FDE organization of several hundred people cannot depend on manager-by-manager onboarding, one-off sessions, and informal access to experts. If learning capacity trails hiring, ramp times would lengthen, standards would diverge, and teams would repeat the same mistakes across regions.

This role will build the programs, teaching network, and systems at the same pace as the organization. Two years from now, success would mean several hundred Deployment Strategists and Applied AI Engineers working from shared standards, learning new capabilities quickly, and improving the system with evidence from customer work.

The Internal Controls function sits within the broader Finance Risk Management (FRM) organization and plays a key role in strengthening the integrity, scalability, and reliability of OpenAI’s finance-critical operations.

Our team designs and governs control frameworks that support accurate, transparent financial results and responsible business execution. We focus on business-process and operational controls across areas such as payments, equity, procure-to-pay, payroll and HR processes, strategic investments, M&A, financial close, third-party dependencies, systems, and other high-risk workflows. We work closely with Controllership, Procurement, Legal, People, Corporate Development, Strategic Finance, Finance Systems, Compliance, and business operators to ensure processes are well-designed, well-documented, and audit-ready.

As part of FRM, we contribute to OpenAI’s overall financial risk posture by supporting audit readiness, third-party risk considerations, operational risk governance, systems oversight, and ongoing process improvement across the finance ecosystem. Together, we help build the foundation of trust and operational clarity needed for OpenAI to scale responsibly.

ABOUT THE ROLE

We’re seeking a Senior Manager, Financial Risk Management to help shape and scale OpenAI’s risk and controls framework across several dynamic business domains. This role will focus on identifying, prioritizing, and mitigating operational and financial risk across areas such as payments, equity, strategic investments, procurement, people processes, systems, third-party dependencies, and other finance-critical workflows.

This person will serve as a senior cross-functional partner to Finance, Controllership, Legal, People, Procurement, Corporate Development, Payments, Systems, and business operators to design and implement controls that are practical, scalable, and capable of holding up in a fast-changing environment with limited structure. The role requires someone with strong technical controls depth who can move fluidly between risk assessment, control design, program governance, and operational execution — translating ambiguous process risk into clear actions teams can adopt.

This role is based in San Francisco, CA. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week and offer relocation assistance to new employees.

IN THIS ROLE, YOU WILL:

- Lead risk and controls support across multiple finance-critical business domains, with a focus on building scalable foundations in a rapidly developing environment.

- Assess risks across payments, equity, procurement flows, strategic investments, people processes and related systems.

- Identify where the control environment is weakest or most exposed, and prioritize the highest-risk areas for remediation, control design, governance, or monitoring support.

- Partner with operational, business, finance, legal, people, procurement, corporate development, and technical teams to design controls that are effective in practice and integrated into day-to-day workflows.

- Translate risks into clear operational requirements, including ownership models, approval points, control objectives, monitoring expectations, reconciliations, evidence needs, system dependencies, and escalation paths.

- Drive cross-functional remediation efforts where processes are unclear, fragmented, overly manual, inconsistently documented, or dependent on immature systems/data.

- Contribute to broader ICFR/SOX and operational risk readiness efforts by strengthening control design, documentation, testing readiness, issue management, and leadership visibility across high-impact processes.

- Experience working in environments with evolving systems, incomplete process structure, unclear ownership, or fragmented data — and bringing order without over-engineering.

- Demonstrated ability to partner effectively with operational, finance, legal, people, procurement, corporate development, and technical teams, including stakeholders who may initially view controls as slowing them down.

- Strong ability to translate broad risks into actionable controls, RCMs, narratives, operating requirements, quality gates, KRIs, dashboards, and remediation plans.

Perplexity is seeking an Applied AI Architect to help our customers turn Perplexity Computer into working solutions that drive measurable impact. This role is ideal for technical, consultative professionals who have led complex software implementations and can move comfortably between customer discovery, solution design, hands-on delivery, and executive communication.

About the role

Perplexity Computer is a new class of AI system that navigates tools, interacts with applications, and completes multi-step workflows end to end. Our customers are using Computer to transform work that traditional software has not been able to address.

Applied AI Architects work directly with customers across presales, onboarding, adoption, and strategic engagements. You will uncover the real business problem, determine what Computer can credibly support, design and configure the workflow, and lead the engagement to a clear outcome.

This is a hands-on, customer-facing role at the intersection of solutions architecture, technical consulting, and program delivery. You will work closely with Sales and Customer Success while serving as a quality filter for requests that require Product or Engineering.

What you'll do

- Lead technical discovery. Work with customer business leaders, technical teams, account executives, and customer success managers to understand the users, current workflow, desired outcome, constraints, and decision-makers.

- Design credible solutions. Map how people, data, tools, approvals, permissions, and decisions interact, then determine how Computer can support the workflow.

- Support complex opportunities. Partner with account executives on technical deal strategy, demos, proofs of value, architecture and security coordination, and engagement scoping.

- Drive value-backed consumption. Identify high-value, repeatable workflows; define the expected business outcomes and usage patterns; and partner with Sales and Customer Success to move customers from technical validation to sustained production use and expansion.

- Build hands-on. Configure, prototype, test, and iterate on Computer skills and workflows, including connectors, permissions, and adjacent tooling.

- Accelerate onboarding and adoption. Provide second-level technical consultation to customer success managers and deliver bounded technical work when customer needs exceed standard Customer Success coverage.

- Run strategic engagements. Establish scope, customer commitments, milestones, success criteria, working cadence, and exit criteria, then lead the work through closure.

- Improve technical escalation. Validate product and engineering needs and produce decision-ready requests with clear evidence, constraints, impact, and acceptance criteria.

- Turn every engagement into leverage. Convert repeated customer needs into reusable workflows, implementation patterns, demos, guidance, and product feedback.

What we're looking for

The strongest Applied AI Architects combine technical depth, consultative problem solving, and disciplined engagement delivery. You should be comfortable working hands-on with the product, advising customer executives, and managing the details required to deliver a successful outcome.

Must-haves

- 5+ years in a customer-facing technical role such as solutions architecture, senior sales engineering, AI implementation, forward deployed work, technical consulting, or technical program leadership.

- Proven consultative discovery skills. You can turn an ambiguous request into a clear business problem, technical approach, and delivery plan.

- Hands-on technical fluency. You are comfortable with APIs, integrations, authentication, identity, permissions, connectors, data flows, and technical troubleshooting.

- Experience delivering complex implementations. You have managed scope, stakeholders, milestones, risk, expectations, and closure.

- Strong solution judgment. You can distinguish education, configuration, implementation, support, product, and engineering problems and recommend the right path.

- Commercial and consumption awareness. You can connect solution design and technical decisions to time to value, usage, credit consumption, customer economics, and expansion potential.

- Executive-credible communication. You can explain technical trade-offs to senior decision-makers while working effectively with practitioners and engineers.

jobs.description:
AIG is reimagining the way we help customers manage risk. Join us as an Analyst in the Data Office department to play your part in that transformation with opportunities to learn and grow your skills and experience as a valued member of the team.

About Us

At AIG, helping organizations and people discover new potential is our purpose. As a global risk leader, we do this for our clients every day. Through our deep expertise in their industries and our innovative solutions that help them smartly manage risk, we enable their growth in ways they never thought possible.

But we also do the same thing for our colleagues, because we know our people are our greatest strength – the source of every insight, every idea and every innovation. When we're working as one team to do what's right for our colleagues and our communities, we can achieve excellence together. We encourage colleagues to give back to the causes they care most about, supporting these efforts through our Volunteer Time Off and Matching Grants Programs.

Make your mark in Data Engineering

Data Engineering plays a critical role in enabling data-driven decision-making across the organization by delivering scalable, reliable, and secure data solutions. This function partners closely with business and technology teams to ensure data is accessible, trustworthy, and positioned to drive innovation, analytics, and operational excellence.

How you will make an impact

When you join AIG, you will be part of a connected cohort community of early career talent participating in a program that equips you with learning experiences and skills needed to launch your career. From day one, you will develop your knowledge and understanding of AIG and the insurance industry and learn new skills through meaningful on-the-job experiences and instructor-led masterclasses. Through exposure to senior leaders, mentoring circles, networking and volunteering, you will build connections with colleagues across the organization. Collectively, these different experiences are designed to enable you to make an impact and build a rewarding and successful career.

Data Engineering Rotation Overview

Data Engineering & Data Architecture: Leverage modern, cloud-based technologies to develop data pipelines that collect, manage, and transform raw data into usable information for business analysis, data science and other analytic use cases. Build modern software systems with Blue/Green Deployment, chaos testing, A/B testing, API and Agents to support the data needs of the customers with adherence to all code/data quality, security, and compliance standards. Familiarity with AWS environment including EMR, Glue, Step Functions; languages like python/pyspark, coding environments like Git and coding assistants like Claude Code, OpenAI Codex, etc. are desirable; but not mandatory.

Minimum Qualifications

Our Early Careers programs are designed for students and recent graduates who are beginning their professional careers, generally within one year of completing their degree.

Education Requirements

• Bachelor’s or Master’s degree to be received no later than June 2027 (unofficial transcript required upon application) in a STEM major or with STEM coursework learned in associated majors. Examples of considered majors include, but are not limited to, Computer Science, Data Engineering, Data Science, Computer Engineering, Software Engineering, Information Systems, Cybersecurity, Mathematics, Applied Mathematics, Statistics, Finance, Economics, Library Science, Geography, or Psychology.

Program Requirements

• Available to start the Program on July 26, 2027.

• Analyst positions are in-person opportunities, requiring employees to work in the office at least four days per week.

Core Qualifications

• Strong written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to communicate effectively in a professional environment.
• Demonstrated analytical, problem-solving, and organizational skills, with strong attention to detail.
• Ability to collaborate effectively, manage multiple priorities, and adapt in a fast-paced, team-oriented environment.

What you’ll need to succeed

AIG seeks candidates who have excelled in previous work experience, demonstrated outstanding academic and extracurricular achievement, possess strong analytical, quantitative and interpersonal skills, and are enthusiastic about learning more about the insurance industry. We also look for a diverse background of experience, culture and thought. Successful candidates typically have a global perspective and a team-oriented track record.

Application Deadline

Applications will be accepted through November 15, 2026, at 11:59 p.m. ET. Applications are reviewed on a rolling basis, and we encourage candidates to apply early. We reserve the right to close this posting prior to the application deadline based on application volume.

Salary for this role is between $86,200 and $103,500

At AIG, we value in-person collaboration as a vital part of our culture, which is why we ask our team members to be primarily in the office. This approach helps us work together effectively and create a supportive, connected environment for our team and clients alike.

Enjoy benefits that take care of what matters

At AIG, our people are our greatest asset. We know how important it is to protect and invest in what’s most important to you. That is why we created our Total Rewards Program, a comprehensive benefits package that extends beyond time spent at work to offer benefits focused on your health, wellbeing and financial security—as well as your professional development—to bring peace of mind to you and your family.

Reimagining insurance to make a bigger difference to the world

American International Group, Inc. (AIG) is a global leader in commercial and personal insurance solutions; we are one of the world’s most far-reaching property casualty networks. It is an exciting time to join us — across our operations, we are thinking in new and innovative ways to deliver ever-better solutions to our customers. At AIG, you can go further to support individuals, businesses, and communities, helping them to manage risk, respond to times of uncertainty and discover new potential. We invest in our largest asset, our people, through continuous learning and development, in a culture that celebrates everyone for who they are and what they want to become.

Welcome to a culture of inclusion

We’re committed to creating a culture that truly respects and celebrates each other’s talents, backgrounds, cultures, opinions and goals. We foster a culture of inclusion and belonging through learning, cultural awareness activities and Employee Resource Groups (ERGs). With global chapters, ERGs are a cornerstone for our culture of inclusion. The talent of our people is one of AIG’s greatest assets, and we are honored that our drive for positive change has been recognized by numerous recent awards and accreditations.

AIG provides equal opportunity to all qualified individuals regardless of race, color, religion, age, gender, gender expression, national origin, veteran status, disability or any other legally protected categories.

AIG is committed to working with and providing reasonable accommodations to job applicants and employees with disabilities. If you believe you need a reasonable accommodation, please send an email to candidatecare@aig.com.
